pageCache.pageTitle: Russet House School - Welcome to Russet House School
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Russet House School
We provide a high quality, specialised education in a happy, purposeful and nurturing environment. We understand the differences experienced by autistic young people (as identified by the Autism Education Trust) in the areas of:
Our curriculum has been developed in recognition of these and so at its core are the life-skills of social communication and self-regulation. Learning is enhanced by a range of specialist and motivating teaching strategies. Behaviour is supported through positive and trauma informed approaches, which are rooted in promoting wellbeing.
If you are looking for a school place for your child, then please visit our admissions page and contact the school office to book a parent tour. We value open communication and collaboration with our parents, working together to identify each child’s next steps and helping them to generalise their learning between home and school.
If you are looking to join our staff team then please follow the link to vacancies. We offer excellent professional development as part of a positive and supportive team. Knowledge and experience of SEND is an advantage but not essential, more important is an interest in children, autism and a readiness to learn in our fast paced-environment.
The Enfield Advisory Service for Autism (EASA) is part of Russet House School, sharing our expertise and experience through a specialist outreach service.
At Russet House School, we believe that everyone can be both a teacher and a learner. We are fully committed to our vision that progress happens when everyone learns and grows together.
Rebecca FreedmanHeadteacher

Russet House School - Helping Others Know Your Child is Autistic
pageCache.text:
Helping Others Know Your Child is Autistic
An Autism alert card and passport scheme, has been introduced across London (September 2019) as a result of a collaboration between the Metropolitan Police Service, City of London Police and British Transport Police.
It has been developed following extensive consultations with individuals with autism and their parents, the National Autistic Society, Autism Partnership Boards, and supported by the National Police Autism Association.
The cards will alert Police officers to the fact that if an individual has autism they may communicate, interact and process information differently to those who do not have autism. In turn, officers will be able to make adjustments and interact with the individual appropriately.
The larger passports will include the same information and can be carried in bags or rucksacks for the individual to produce if required.
For further reading, please use this link: Launch of Autism Alert Cards
To receive a card & passport for your child or others you may know who have autism, please send your full postal address in an email to: Autism@met.police.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: Russet House School - Supporting Pupils Regulation
pageCache.text:
Supporting pupils regulation
Russet House follows the PRICE Training syllabus to ensure staff are knowledgeable and confident to support our pupils with behaviours of challenge. We have 5 in-house PRICE instructors and all permanent members of class staff are trained within their first year at the school. Please see the leaflet below from PRICE, which explains more about their theoretical basis and techniques.
All behaviour interventions are carried out in-line with the School’s Positive Behaviour Support Policy.
Please click here for more information about PRICE training

pageCache.pageTitle: Russet House School - Education, Health & Care Plan
pageCache.text:
Education, Health and Care Plans
All pupils at Russet House School have an Education Health and Care Plan (EHCP) or are in process of getting one supported by the school.
Annual Review of an Education Health and Care Plan
Each pupil’s Educational, Health and Care Plan is reviewed annually at the Annual Review of the EHCP meeting. This is chaired by the Phase Leader and attended by the child’s parent/s, Class Teacher and other professionals as appropriate. At the meeting the parent/s, class teacher and Phase Leader discuss the child’s progress towards the outcomes in his/ her EHCP and agree new outcomes; these focus on the areas of priority for each child.
Parents need to check their child’s EHCP, parts A1 and A2 before the Annual Review meeting, and make any changes they wish by writing it on the document.

pageCache.pageTitle: Russet House School - School Meals and Healthy Eating
pageCache.text:
School Meals and Healthy Eating
Nut awareness notice
Russet House school is a food allergy aware school. We have children in school with severe nut allergies and it is vital that we keep them as safe as possible. Please do not send any items containing nuts in to school for your child for snacks or packed lunches. Also please do not bring any items containing nuts on to our school site. Thank you.
Russet House has a kitchen on site where meals are prepared and served.
Stir Food provide the school meals, and use quality ingredients. Menus are nutritionally balanced and include seasonal and locally sourced produce.
Please let us know if your child has any special dietary requirements such as gluten or dairy-free.
Please click here to view our school menu
Our meals are freshly cooked daily by qualified and fully trained staff. All Kitchen Supervisors are trained to at least the level of NVQ2 in Food Preparation and Cooking and many hold qualifications in Customer Care and Team Leadership.
Some children are entitled to a free school meal because of the benefits their parents receive.
If you think your child may be entitled to a free school meal for this reason, please speak to our school office or call the Pupil Benefit Helpline on 020 8379 5367 (8.30am – 12pm then 2pm – 4pm).

pageCache.pageTitle: Russet House School - Student Placements And Work Experience
pageCache.text:
Student Placements And Work Experience
We do provide placements for 18 years old and over but this is dependent on a number of factors including
In order to be equitable, no more than 2 students from any single establishment will be offered places at the same time.
Where possible all student teachers (GTP, PGCE,Schools Direct) will be given priority for placements.
Students studying for TA courses, CACHE diploma, GNVQ III or BTEC qualification will be considered in their second year of training as their special interest placement.
Students considered for a placement will be invited to attend RHS for a pre-placement visit to ensure that they have a good understanding of the demands of this setting.
During the visit they will have a brief tour of the school, and explanation of the children’s needs, and the approaches used by staff.
If there are concerns about the suitability of the placement either from the student or the RHS representative, we will liaise with the applicant's tutor (where applicable) to discuss the matter.
The student will be given an information pack including the following:
Experience & maturity of student
Time of year
Couse being studied (if relevant)
Preferred age range (for teaching practice)
RHS Staffing levels
Autism handout
Key Makaton signs/symbols
